alt: Paper 3 lasts 2 hours 15 minutes for 60 marks. Section A, Listening Comprehension, has 30 marks and a recommended 45 minutes; Section B, Listening, Reading and Writing, has 30 marks and a recommended 1 hour 30 minutes. The time bar is drawn to scale.
caption: Two sections with equal marks, but Section B gets twice the recommended time.

alt: Paper 1 tests translation into English, reading comprehension and research-question writing; Paper 2 tests translation into Urdu and written response to works; Paper 3 combines listening, reading and writing without translation. Strength at translation does not transfer automatically to listening.
caption: Paper 3 completes the four skills; translation practice alone will not prepare you for it.

alt: A scale from formal, news-style Urdu to conversational spoken Urdu, with news broadcasts, interviews and spoken narrative along it. Practise across speed and register, and read each question before the audio plays where the format allows.
caption: Listen across registers, and read the question first so you know what to listen for.

alt: Four linked steps for Section B: listen to or read the source, take accurate notes, use those notes to build the answer, and write the response. Treating Section B as an afterthought leaves half the marks under-practised.
caption: Practise note-taking and writing as one skill, under the same timing.

alt: For Section A: when a detail is missed, note roughly where it fell, finish the passage, then replay just that section, rather than replaying whole passages. Rehearse with pausable audio inside 45 minutes, then practise full timed sittings.
caption: Replay just the section you missed, and keep inside the 45 minutes.
